institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Crucial that the destination was close to Denmark, that it was a smaller city with nature close by, and that the culture was similar to Denmark. The academic level had to be the same or similar to UCPH. There had to be oppertunities to go hiking in the mountains for day or weekend trips.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. Both UCPH and the host institution (NTNU) provided sufficient information by mail upon arrival. NTNU had many guides on their homepage for exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, but it was easy to get around in the city, and all necessary information about the intro-week and course registration was send to us by mail from NTNU.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was more difficult to find housing than expected. Rooms in student villages can be wished upon formally applying for a spot at the host university. But it does not seems as if the Nordic students are "prioritized" for such student accommodation.
Privat housing - typically with Norwegian students - can be found at
Finn.no
or
Hybel.no
. In the end everyone manages to find a decent accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Start looking for accommodation earlier than you think. Before or in the beginning of the summer holiday. A lot of rooms are posted on
Finn.no
and
Hybel.no
throughout the summerbreak, but there are also a lot of exchange students looking for accommodation. When you find a room, look up the address in Maps, if possible. The city is not that large, but there are many hills and public transportation can take time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Upon arrival to the host institution, exchange students are provided with a login to "Studentweb". From here it is relatively easy and intuitive to register for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write an email to the exchange office, but the whole course registration process is easy and mails are send to guide the students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: A was able to register for all the courses I initially wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None, it really is intuitive and easy. Just remember the date for last registration of courses, but this will also be send by mail from the host institution.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Courses were divided into Intermediate (BA level) and Second degree level (MA level).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar, with a lot of normal lectures and some, but not a lot, of group work. For some courses there were mandatory work, such as presentations of articles or midterm assignments, that needed to be passed in order to be eligable to take the exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MOL3000: Introduction to Molecular Medicine (MA level).
MOL3023: Molecular Medical Bacteriology (MA level)
TMMT4001: Sustainable Food Production (MA level)
INTRO175: Introduction to Norway (BA level)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
MOL3023 was very interesting as it connected knowledge of bacteria to disease outbreak and surveillance, providing the clinical and medical aspect of infection with bacteria. Lectures were given on some selected bacteria such as streptococcus, staphylococcus, tuberculosis and E. Coli. The teaching consisted mainly of lectures and one midterm assignment in bioinformatics. But not to worry if you do not know anything of bioinformatics. The aim of the assignment was to become familiarized with the field, and I really learned a lot from it.

MOL3000 was also really interesting with various subjects from the human genome, mutations and inherited disease to diabetes and some bioinformatics as well. The teaching consisted mainly of lectures and one mandatory presentation of an article within one of the subjects.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Generally, food was more expensive than in Denmark, but that was to be expected.

A note to the costs; Internet was a part of my rent and I had no phone bill due to too much data being used. This is not the case for everyone.
The expenses for trips was also more expensive in the first months, and less expensive from november when it got colder and exams were approaching.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The university has a sports club called NTNUI. Here, students can sign up for all sorts of sports including swimming, badminton, kayak and soccer. Students can also sign up for SiT to be able to train at the gym. 

The students in Trondheim can become a member of Studentersamfundet, which is a large building where events and other festivities are held throughout the semester.

ESN (Europen Student Network) is an organisation outside the university where exchange students can participate in events and come on trips during the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend that you sign up for some sports in NTNUI. If you are keen on hiking, Ski and Fjellsport arranges tours almost every weekend, with variyng difficulty. The destination depends on the trip coordinators, but they arrange hiking trips with tent or overnight in cabins owned by the university, ice skating trips, snowshoe trips and many other kind of tours. 
I would also recommend signing up for SiT.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend that you take some walks in the city to see the fortress (Kristianfestningen) and walk along the Ladestien, where there is also a nice little beach.
Bymarka is a forrest very close to the city, where there are endless of hiking oppertunities for day-trips. It is very easy to get from the city and into the forrest. The highest top is 565 moh and provides great views over the city and to the mountains in the distance. In the fall semester, if you are lucky, snow will fall in late november/early december and you will be able to go cross country skiing. 
I would also recommend taking a ferry from Trondheim to Fosen for a day or weekend hike. 

For longer trips, I would recommend taking the train (or a car) down to Dovrefjell, rent a cabin and go on hikes. It might be advantageous to become member of DNT, as they own a lot of cabins all over Norway. It is also a good idea to plan a trip around some of these cabins, doing cabin-to-cabin hikes, where you really find yourself in the middle of nowhere in the mountains.
ESN plans multiple trips during the semester, one going to Lofoten. I would definitely recommend going to Lofoten, but plan the trip yourself. It is easy taking the train from Trondheim to Bodø and from there a ferry to Lofoten (Moskenes or Svolvær). Rent a car in Bodø and take on the ferry. Go no later than september.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is very similar to Denmark, so it was easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Look for private accommodation with Norwegian students, and engage in activities provided by the university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Difficult to answer as the culture is so similar to Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Engage yourself in sports in NTNUI and events in at the university or in the city.
Embrace the norwegian, take an oppertunity to learn more of the language.
Take advantage of the nature and mountains being so close to the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of other danish exchange students that had the same interests and wanted to go on hikes and tours together, and join different events in the city. Sharing great experiences together, and taking new friendships and memories back home with us.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Wanting to see and experience as much of the norwegian nature as possible, but not having enough time. It was a bit stressfull to have so many ideas for tours and wanting to go every weekend, but still remembering that we had courses to attend and exams to pass.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Adjust your expectations before going abroad. Remember that Norway is not far away, and you can come back and do that trip you did not have time for at a later time. You may meet exchange students that are more interested in becoming involved in student organizations, or some that want to spend all their time exploring the mountains. Find out what it is that you want to gain from this experience and pursue it, but do not set your expectations unrealistically high. You do not want to end up being disappointed, or being stressed out about all the things you want to do before leaving again.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
